placements.note: site:fermilab-main-campus is an existing record owned by another lead, already used for several other Fermilab short-baseline detector placements without a hall-specific coordinate; referenced here, not created.
placements.quote: The neutrino beam was created using 800 GeV protons from the Fermilab Tevatron interacting in a meter long tungsten beam dump ... The emulsion targets were exposed from April to September 1997.

summary.plain: A stack of nuclear-emulsion sheets and iron plates, backed by electronic trackers, that caught tau neutrinos as they interacted -- the first detector ever to do so directly.
summary.technical: Hybrid emulsion-target (nuclear-emulsion sheets interspersed with steel/iron sheets, an emulsion-cloud-chamber-style target) followed by electronic scintillator counters and drift-chamber spectrometers, at a Tevatron fixed-target beam dump.

technology.locator: arXiv:hep-ex/0012035 (Phys. Lett. B 504 (2001) 218), detector and beam description
technology.note: Detector description from the DONUT 2001 paper (arXiv:hep-ex/0012035): nuclear emulsion with stainless steel sheets (ECC modules), scintillation counter veto wall, scintillating-fibre tracker, hodoscopes and drift chambers.
technology.quote: Nuclear emulsion was used to locate and resolve these decays. ... stainless steel sheets interleaved with emulsion plates ... scintillation counter veto wall ... Tracks in the SFT were projected downstream to those in drift chambers
technology.value: Nuclear-emulsion target with interspersed steel sheets, combined with electronic scintillator counters and drift chambers
